about.title: Chino Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Chino sits where the Pomona Freeway meets a grid of busy surface streets, and the collision numbers reflect that traffic. In 2025, the most recent final reporting year, the city logged 400 injury collisions that left 571 people hurt and claimed 7 lives. Public records show SR-60, Central Avenue, Riverside Drive and Euclid Avenue carry the highest crash counts, with reports clustering on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. If one of those crashes was yours, the days that follow can feel scattered: a damaged car, medical appointments, an adjuster calling early. LawProactive exists for that moment. We are not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Chino residents with an independent personal injury attorney who handles car accident claims in San Bernardino County. That attorney works on contingency, so there is no fee unless your case recovers money. Our role is simply to help you find someone to talk to before the insurer shapes the story.

whyChoose.title: Why Chino Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Deadlines are shorter than people expect
items.desc: California gives you two years to file most car accident claims, but if a city, county, or state vehicle was involved, a claim may need to be filed in as little as six months. An early conversation keeps those dates from slipping past.

items.title: Partial fault does not end your claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover even if you share some blame; your recovery is simply reduced by your percentage. An attorney can push back when an insurer tries to inflate your share.

items.title: Evidence and your words matter early
items.desc: Photos, witness names, and repair records fade fast, and the other driver's insurer may ask for a recorded statement before you understand your injuries. Connecting with counsel first helps protect both.

items.question: My crash was on SR-60 in Chino. Does that change anything about my claim?
items.answer: Freeway collisions are often handled by the CHP rather than Chino police, so your report will come from a different agency, and multi-vehicle chain reactions on the Pomona Freeway can make fault more complicated. If a state or Caltrans vehicle was involved, or a road condition played a role, a government claim deadline as short as six months may apply. An attorney can sort out which agency and which timeline you are dealing with.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are generally not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and doing so before you know the full extent of your injuries can work against you. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that minimize claims. Most attorneys prefer you speak with them first, and LawProactive can connect you with one at no cost.

items.question: I think I was partly at fault. Can I still recover for my injuries?
items.answer: Yes. California uses pure comparative fault, so even someone found mostly responsible can still recover the portion of damages attributed to the other party. Your compensation is reduced by your share of blame rather than eliminated. There is also no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in a standard car accident case.
